query_text: What exactly is happening when someone experiences déjà vu?

messages.content: What exactly is happening when someone experiences déjà vu?

message.content:
Déjà vu is the *false feeling of familiarity*—your brain interprets a present moment as if it has happened before, even though it hasn’t. Most explanations point to a brief mismatch in memory processing, where perception and recall get slightly out of sync.[1][2]

Common theories include:
- **Split perception / divided attention:** you may have taken in part of the scene earlier without fully noticing it, so it later feels like a repeat.[1][2]
- **Memory-processing mix-up:** the brain may tag a new experience as a memory because familiarity and recall signals fire at the wrong time.[1][2]
- **Delayed or duplicated processing:** the same input may reach memory systems by two routes or at two slightly different times, creating a “seen this already” effect.[1][3]
- **Similarity to a forgotten experience:** a current situation may closely resemble something you encountered before but can’t consciously remember.[1][3]

In most people, déjà vu is *brief and harmless*.[2] But if it happens very often or is accompanied by other symptoms, it can sometimes be linked to neurological conditions such as *temporal lobe epilepsy*.[2][3]
